args.text: When a description says one participant sends information or a message to another participant, model the communication using an appropriate BPMN message-flow element or communication activity, rather than treating the send as an ordinary task.

trace.reason: The records show the described sending action represented as a generated sendTask where the reference has a task; check related documented guidance before deciding whether this element-type choice supports a guideline.

result.rule: Distinguish message tasks from message events: a task models performed work; an event models a message occurrence affecting flow.
Create bpmn:collaboration when distinct participants interact and represent every participant as a bpmn:participant pool.
Use bpmn:sendTask or bpmn:receiveTask when sending or waiting for a message is itself the modeled unit of work.
Create reusable bpmn:message elements and messageRef only when communication content or shared message identity matters.
When the description does not justify a specialized construct, use the simplest compatible BPMN construct and do not guess missing semantics.
Model every distinct activity, event, participant, decision, branch, loop, message and outcome stated in the description. Do not invent process facts.

args.text: When the description states that one participant sends a message to another, model the sending work as a BPMN sendTask when sending the message is itself the activity.

trace.reason: Check whether an error-driven guideline already covers the sendTask choice evidenced by the generated extra element.

result.rule: When the description says that a participant performs work by sending information to another participant: Model the sending as a task (use a send task when sending is itself the unit of work). Represent communication separately where appropriate; do not attach a message event definition to a task.

When the description describes communication or a signal between participants, while the underlying work or the receipt of that communication is already represented by activities or events: model the communication with a message flow between the appropriate existing sender and receiver nodes; do not add separate send or receive tasks solely to represent the exchange, or create message flows for physical movement that is not described as communication

When the description states that a participant performs an action that initiates the process: Model the described action as a task in the process flow; do not also represent that same action as a start event.

When the description identifies an external system or organization as a sender or recipient of information exchanged with the process: model it as a separate participant and represent the described exchanges with message flows between the participants, not solely with events inside one process

args.text: When the description states alternative outcomes or says that one of several actions may occur, model the choice with an exclusive gateway before the alternative branches, then route each branch to its corresponding outcome.

trace.reason: Check whether a guideline already covers how to model the explicit either/or outcomes, before proposing a rule.

result.rule: Several unconditional outgoing flows from one activity can all proceed. Use a gateway when the description requires a decision or synchronization.
Allow multiple start or end events when the description has distinct triggers or outcomes. Do not force all outcomes into one end.
Model every distinct activity, event, participant, decision, branch, loop, message and outcome stated in the description. Do not invent process facts.
Use an event-based gateway when the first occurring event selects the path. Target supported catching events or receive tasks, not ordinary tasks.
Use transaction, ad-hoc or compensation behavior only when its specific semantics are explicitly described.
Use a complex gateway only for an explicitly described rule that XOR, OR and AND cannot express. Prefer separate split and join gateways for clarity.
